The Osmotic Expanse

Picture Book · v3 · the six lineages and every creature of the Lytic Bestiary

LineagesOrder I: Lytic SwarmsOrder II: Protein SentinelsOrder III: Nutrient DriftersOrder IV: Pathogenic WraithsOrder V: Osmotic BrutesOrder VI: Immune SentinelsOrder VII: Anomalies

Everyone in this world is a single living cell the size of a person. The six lineages are the peoples you can play. The creatures are what you meet. Numbers are kept small and last: this is a book for looking.

The six lineages

The peoples of the Expanse. You choose one when you make a character.

Amoeban

No wall you did not choose. Amoebans flow: a body is a temporary decision, and they are the only lineage that finds that normal. They are the Expanse's chemists, digesters, and thieves, and every other lineage has a word for an Amoeban that means "honest in the worst way".

Gift. once per scene, as a 1-PP action, alter your shape: pass a gap of one Drift, hide one Apparatus inside yourself, change your apparent size class by one, or mimic a phenotype you have touched (not a person — a type). Lasts until you Reshape again.

Frailty. your grafts are 50% less reliable. Any graft you install takes one extra Slot, and Testate grafts cannot be worn at all.

Epithalian

Epithalians are sheet-beings: they grow in layers, they build in sheets, and they understand instinctively that a wall is a moral position. Colony architects, foundry masters, and the people who sign the toll contracts. They are the lineage most other organisms look at and call civilisation.

Gift. once per scene, as a Reactive (spend your Reserve), reduce incoming damage by 6 + your Stage and end one Leaking effect on yourself or an adjacent ally.

Frailty. your shape is decided early. You cannot benefit from Metamorphosis resets, and any condition that changes shape (Turgid, Flaccid) lasts one extra Cycle.

Flagellan

Born in the Great Flows. Flagellans move or they sulk; a stationary Flagellan is a sick one. They are couriers, herders of drift-herds, navigators, and the only lineage that reads a current the way an Epithalian reads a wall.

Gift. once per scene, declare a line of fluid anywhere you can smell or see: for the next 2 Cycles, you and any ally touching that line gain +1 PP and +2 Drifts, and one Osmotic effect you create along it costs 0 ATP.

Frailty. if you begin a Pulse Cycle having not moved since your last turn, you gain no PP that Cycle (only Reactive Osmosis is available). In a Reconstitution you must spend at least one Fugue Interval moving.

Rides It Out (v3). A rolled 1 marks Stress only three times in four.

Lysosan

The viral lineage — not infected, bilateral. A Lysosan carries sequences that are not theirs and has negotiated with them. They are the Expanse's information brokers, spies, geneticists, and the only beings who can lie to an antigen scan. Other lineages cannot decide whether they are people or a very political library.

Gift. once per scene, when an effect would impose a condition on you, choose instead to carry it: nothing happens now, but at any later point you may give that condition to another organism (Contact or via a projectile action, 1 PP) or burn it for +2 dice on your next roll. You cannot carry more than two at once.

Frailty. every Immune Sentinel, Warden ward, and antigen gate in the Expanse can see that you are not quite standard. Social contests with Immunans start one rung worse on the Stakes Ladder, and you cannot hold the Antigen Hood graft.

Immunan

Immunans are the lineage of recognising: they mark, they rank, they remember what belonged and what did not. They staff the Warden Circles, keep the antigen registers, and are the only beings who can look at a Lysosan and name every sequence it carries. They are also, in the estimation of everyone else, incapable of a metaphor.

Gift. once per scene, declare one organism within Mid band self or not-self. While self, allies' effects against it count as friendly and its soak increases by 2; while not-self, it is Marked and all attacks against it by your Cohort gain +1 die.

Frailty. you cannot be deceived by language alone, but you also cannot use it: disadvantage on all deceptive (Affective/Deceptive register) contests, and you always answer a question truthfully unless an Oath forbids it (which physically hurts: 1 Stress per sentence).

Barophil

Extremophiles: the lineages that chose the worst places and did fine. Barophils live in acid, in pressure, in heat, and in cold so deep that thought slows. They measure time in tides and patience in epochs, and they are the only beings that the Vacuolar Abyss considers weather rather than intruders.

Gift. you ignore one tonic state of your choice at all times (choose at creation; may be changed at each Stage transition). Additionally, hazard and environmental damage against you is reduced by 2 × your Stage.

Frailty. your Frequency Check is always made at −2, and your Reactive Osmosis costs 2 PP.

Order I: Lytic Swarms

Hunger that learned to move. They dissolve things before eating them.

Standard · Tier 1

Cytoplasmic Bleeder

In a fight: finds the slowest organism, attaches, and lets its allies do the killing.

Weak point: Detach is one OSM contest (AT 14) or a Thermal/Lytic burn; Phagocyte Engulfment is fatal.

Weak point: if you deny it corpses (burn them, salt them, take them) it becomes a nuisance instead of a threat.

In a fight: it is a force multiplier with legs. Fights escalate around it.

Weak point: kill it early (its specials are expensive and it has mediocre soak for its tier); Desiccation and Cold end its field; silence gear (Signal Dampener) denies its Broadcast.

Standard · T3 · Mesoscopic · MT 15 · MI 38 · soak 3 · BD 4 Voltaic · pool 6d · PP 3 · Flow 4
Standard · Tier 4

Graft Inquisitor

In a fight: reads you, names what is illegal about you, and then fights with the law already on its side.

Weak point: be lawful (the Cohort's best defence is paperwork), or win in three Cycles (it has only 3 PP and one big special).

Standard · T4 · Mesoscopic · MT 16 · MI 46 · soak 4 · BD 5 Kinetic · pool 7d · PP 3 · Flow 4
Elite · Tier 4

Inflammatory Tempest

In a fight: arrives, makes the region unlivable, and drowns the Cohort in bodies.

Weak point: it cannot stop recruiting, which means it cannot be flanked usefully — but its own reinforcements block its lines of effect. Cold, Desiccation, and any Dry zone end Fevered Ground; a Navigator's shear can turn its push against it. It burns its own allies: it is on bad terms with every other Order.

Elite · T4 · Vast · MT 17 · MI 92 · soak 6 · BD 6 Thermal · pool 8d · PP 4 · Flow 5
Elite · Tier 5

Tolerance Priest

In a fight: does not fight. Reclassifies.

Weak point: it must speak: Silence gear, a Counter-Signal, or killing it in two Cycles (it has no armour, no brace, and its Flow is only 4). Its power depends on there being Sentinels nearby: fight it where the state is absent, and it is a soft old thing with very high MI.

Elite · T5 · Mesoscopic, unarmoured, unsettlingly gentle · MT 18 · MI 108 · soak 7 · BD 7 Genetic · pool 9d · PP 4 · Flow 4

The Quiet

Weak point: Phase 3. It cannot act then, and whatever it asks is answerable: the Cohort's honest answers end the encounter in their favour. This is a fight that the table should be allowed to win by talking, and it will be the best scene of the campaign.

Catastrophe · Tier 5

Curator Manifestation

In a fight: arrives late, uninvited, and unkillable. It resolves the encounter. Your job as Director is to make it interesting rather than fatal: it has a policy, and policies have preferences.

Weak point: Apotheosis. A Cohort at Core Clock 5 with Apotheotic Choices can contest its Thresholds at AT 28 (Nucleoid) and, on a Runaway Catalysis, force it to ask a question instead of acting — which is the closest thing to a wound a Curator has.

Catastrophe · T5 (Apotheotic) · size: too large to be in the water · MT 15 · MI 110 / 110 / 110 (three phases; it does not go Dormant, it files the phase) · soak 9 · BD 9 Genetic · pool 10d · PP 5 · Flow 3

The Long Echo
